page: Microsoft Azure B32s_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, supplying 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with two threads per core. Architectural features include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a 48 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The configuration includes 128.0 GB of main memory, equating to 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, and it does not contain discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced mid-tier compute capabilities across integer, cryptographic, and compilation suites. The server recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 13784.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 36914.38, while static web serving throughput reached 33.25 GB/sec. Memory subsystem evaluation reveals upper-tier responsiveness, marked by a PassMark memory score of 2828.58 and cached small-block read bandwidth of 1667.43 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance produced 31.14 million Redis SET operations per second and handled text generation on a 135M parameter LLM at 290.9 tokens per second, though large-model (70B) prompt execution registered at a lower tier of 6.61 tokens per second.

Utilizing a burstable processor allocation model, the B32s_v2 provides favorable cost efficiency for resource-dense workloads that experience intermittent spikes rather than continuous maximum CPU utilization. The lack of onboard local disk means that persistence depends entirely on remote volume attachments. The hardware balance makes the instance suitable for software compilation pipelines, testing and staging databases, batch ETL jobs, and variable-load web service deployments.
description: Microsoft Azure B32s_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine provisioned with 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Accompanied by 128.0 GB of system memory, it follows a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, though it includes neither local storage disks nor dedicated GPU hardware. Synthetic testing reflects steady middle-tier multi-core computing capacity alongside strong memory subsystem throughput, highlighted by a PassMark memory score in the upper quartile and 31.14 million Redis SET operations per second. Because it operates on burstable CPU scheduling, the system yields cost-effective resource density for intermittent computational demands rather than constant high-load execution. It is suited for CI/CD compilation runners, relational database staging, batch processing, and non-sustained enterprise application hosting.
